title: AgentCollab: A Self-Evaluation-Driven Collaboration Paradigm for Efficient LLM Agents
abstract: arXiv:2603.26034v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Autonomous agents powered by large language models (LLMs) perform complex tasks through long-horizon reasoning and tool interaction, where a fundamental trade-off arises between execution efficiency and reasoning robustness. Models at different capability-cost levels offer complementary advantages: lower-cost models enable fast execution but may struggle on difficult reasoning segments, while stronger models provide more robust reasoning at higher computational cost. We present AgentCollab, a self-driven collaborative inference framework that dynamically coordinates models with different reasoning capacities during agent execution. Instead of relying on external routing modules, the framework uses the agent's own self-reflection signal to determine whether the current reasoning trajectory is making meaningful progress, and escalates control to a stronger reasoning tier only when necessary. translated_title: AgentCollab：一种由自我评估驱动的LLM智能体高效协作范式
translated_abstract: 由大语言模型（LLM）驱动的自主智能体通过长程推理和工具交互来执行复杂任务，其中执行效率与推理鲁棒性之间存在根本性的权衡。处于不同能力-成本层级的模型具有互补优势：较低成本的模型能够快速执行，但在困难的推理片段上可能表现不佳，而更强的模型能以更高的计算成本提供更鲁棒的推理。我们提出了AgentCollab，这是一个自驱动的协作推理框架，可在智能体执行过程中动态协调具有不同推理能力的模型。该框架不依赖外部路由模块，而是利用智能体自身的自反思信号来判断当前推理轨迹是否正在取得实质性进展，并且仅在必要时才将控制权升级至更强的推理层级。为了进一步稳定长程执行，
tldr: AgentCollab提出了一种由自评估驱动的协作推理框架，利用智能体自身的反思信号动态协调不同能力级别的LLM模型，仅在必要时才升级至更强的推理层级，从而在执行效率与推理鲁棒性之间取得平衡。
en_tdlr: AgentCollab introduces a self-evaluation-driven collaborative inference framework that uses the agent's own self-reflection signals to dynamically coordinate LLMs of different reasoning capacities, escalating to stronger reasoning tiers only when necessary, thereby balancing execution efficiency and reasoning robustness.
